whatItIs.text: Split, hulled lentils that cook fast and collapse into a thick, golden dal or soup — the quickest-cooking lentil in the pantry.

historyNote.text: The lentil gave English two words: the Latin lens named a Roman family, Lentulus, and gave optical lenses their name; in the Indian subcontinent split lentils are dal, a staple cooked with rice or roti.

howToChoose.text: Choose even, unbroken seeds with a fresh starchy smell; red lentils need no soaking, but rinsing off dust is worth the ten seconds.

storage.text: Keep dry and airtight in a cool cupboard.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: Soft lentils thicken soups and curries, mash into fritters with egg and spice, or become a 20-minute dal — the easiest dinner in the pantry.

substitutions.ratio: up to 1/3 of flour in flatbreads
